SOLVING CRIME WITH DNA PHENOTYPING AND ANCESTRY

By: Eugene Botha | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
....reconstructing a murderer's face by just using hi DNA

Unique Selling Point:
Cutting edge new technology and new use of DNA

Summary:
DNA Phenotyping is a new tool in forensics, and is the prediction of physical appearance from DNA. It can be used to generate leads in cases where there are no suspects or database hits, to narrow suspect lists, and to help solve human remains cases. Whereas traditional DNA forensics matches STRs from a sample to a known suspect or a database, DNA phenotyping can generate new leads about an individual, even if they have not previously been identified in a database.

Further information:
DNA Phenotyping is the prediction of physical appearance from DNA. It can be used to generate leads in cases where there are no suspects or database hits, to narrow suspect lists, and to help solve human remains cases. Whereas traditional DNA forensics matches STRs from a sample to a known suspect or a database, DNA phenotyping can generate new leads about an individual, even if they have not previously been identified in a database. DNA phenotyping takes advantage of modern SNP technology to read the parts of the genome that actually code for the differences between people. The Snapshot DNA Phenotyping System translates SNP information from an unknown individual's DNA sample into predictions of ancestry and physical appearance traits, such as skin color, hair color, eye color, freckling, and even face morphology. Each phenotype prediction is made with a measure of confidence, including those that can be excluded with high confidence. SNP Technology. Recent advances in genomic technology have made it practical and affordable to read the sequence of millions of pieces of DNA from a small quantity of sample. This data captures a large proportion of the genomic variation between people and thus contains much of the genetic blueprint that differentiates people's appearance. These SNP genotypes can then be paired with phenotypes from thousands of subjects to create a genotype-and-phenotype (GaP) dataset for analysis.

DNA Matching is a powerful feature that uses your DNA to help you find relatives. The technology compares your DNA data with the DNA data of others, and identifies shared genetic sequences that indicate a possible family relationship. The higher the percentage of DNA that you have in common with another person, the closer your likely relationship.

All of this is now being used in the fight against crime and has been solving decades old cold cases over the last few months.

Parabon NanoLabs, Inc. is a vertically integrated DNA technology company that develops next-generation therapeutic and forensic products, which leverage the enormous power of DNA. Staffed by a uniquely qualified team of scientists and technologists, with expertise ranging from bioinformatics and oncology to chemistry and computer science, the Company is bringing to market revolutionary new products and services made possible by recent advances in DNA sequencing, processing and manufacturing technologies.

The are also the leaders in DNA sequencing and forensics and have developed the snapshot technology. Snapshot is a cutting-edge forensic DNA analysis service that provides a variety of tools for solving hard cases quickly:
* Genetic Genealogy: Identify a subject by matching their DNA to one or more family members.
* DNA Phenotyping: Predict physical appearance and ancestry of an unknown person from their DNA.
* Kinship Inference: Determine kinship between DNA samples out to six degrees of relatedness.

Snapshot is ideal for generating investigative leads, narrowing suspect lists, and solving human remains cases, without wasting time and money chasing false leads.

We will also test the Snapshot technology by supplying them with DNA form Devi and see how they reconstruct the face.

To make it local, we will also have Lobo das Neves to comment on the technology.


Extra Budget Items:
Cost of Snapshot analysis.

Press Release:


DNA Forensics
In the enduring fight against crime, a new scientific weapon has entered the fray. DNA Phenotyping is a new tool in forensics which could help police investigators determine a suspect’s physical appearance using just their DNA. It’s been hailed as a remarkable development, but can DNA Phenotyping really help pin-point the identity of an unknown assailant? Carte Blanche puts it to the test.
Producer: Eugene Botha
Presenter: Devi Sankaree Govender


Script:


V/O:
Imagine a crime scene where a woman was stabbed, and her office ransacked. The police are investigating, and the only clue they find is a tiny bit foreign DNA under one of the victim’s nails when she scratched the unknown perpetrator.

Would it not be great if the DNA could be used to create a snapshot of the killer – down to their eye and hair colour?
LINK:
Science fiction? It used to be, but not anymore. A company in the United States have begun to use DNA in a revolutionary fashion in the fight against crime.
V/O:
International law enforcement expert Lobo das Neves says these new advances in using DNA is revolutionizing the fight against crime.
Lobo:
Cases are now being solved that would never have been solved before.
Devi:
When DNA analysis first arrived it revolutionized forensic, didn’t it?
Lobo:
It enabled us to identify a specific suspect to a specific event or a specific crime and that DNA could identify that person beyond any question.
Devi:
But DNA also has its limitations.
Lobo:
Well DNA has limitations. It is similar to a fingerprint in a case where you find DNA evidence on a scene or fingerprint evidence on a scene it does not give you the identity of the suspect if that suspect’s DNA or finger print is not already on record.
V/O:
But that has now changed. We know DNA is the blue-print for everything that makes us human – it determines everything about us, including what we look like.

Now a company in the US is claiming that they have developed technology that enables them to use just DNA to predict the appearance of an unknown perpetrator of a crime. And all they require is a sample of DNA.
LINK:
These claims sound so incredible that we decided to put these claims to the test with me as the guinea-pig.
V/O:
We took four samples of my DNA a few weeks ago by simply swabbing the insides of my cheeks.
Devi:
So this is the test swab. It looks like and earbud…. Here goes.
V/O:
We did three more swabs and sent it off to the United States to be analysed. The company received no information on me. All they knew is that it is DNA from Africa. Steven Armentrout is the CEO of Parabon Nanolabs.
Steven:
In 2010 a Government tender was put forth that was asking for phenotyping as a tool to predict from DNA appearance and ancestry. Can a team reverse engineer the genome and figure out what genes code for eye colour and hair colour and so forth. We bid on that tender and were given the award.
LINK:
For five years they did intense research to find out which genes code for hair, skin and eye colour, and various facial features.
Steven
With a large enough database and machine learning algorithms we were eventually able to create models to predict those traits along with ancestry. So in 2015, even though this began as a Department of Defence effort, we began to offer it to law enforcement for use in casework.
V/O:
Ellen McRae Greytak is the Director of Bioinformatics at the company.
Ellen:
When we first started this it wasn’t clear whether anything beyond light versus dark eyes could be predicted with any accuracy. We thought there should be more that can be predicted because we know these traits are being passed down through families because the DNA is being passed down through families. So, it was just a matter of figuring out what parts of the DNA code for each of these features. So we were able to show that it is possible to get accurate predictions of eye colour, hair colour, skin colour, freckling, and produce a relatively reasonable image of that person’s face. We can predict that person’s face shape in a way that will strongly resemble them and figure out what is unique about that person’s face.
V/O:
They are also able to determine a person’s genetic heritage and indicate where someone’s ancestors are from. They can reliably tell if a person’s ancestors are from Europe or Asia or Africa. And they can even distinguish between Northern European or Southern European, or between Central Asia or East Asia.
LINK:
This was a staggering breakthrough and holds enormous potential for police investigations.
Steven
This is very helpful for narrowing down suspect lists, excluding people from investigations. Absent that kind of information police might be inclined to investigate everyone that comes across their desk. But in fact if we are able to give them very detailed ancestry, predictions of hair colour, eye colour, skin colour, freckling, face shape. These are all phenotypes that we predict with high accuracy and with that snapshot information they are now being able to be much more efficient.
V/O:
Once the DNA analysis is done, they know the basics of a person. All of this then go to an artist who uses the DNA results to construct an image from a very basic face shape.
Ellen:
So we make this prediction using this person’s sex and thousands and thousands of unique snips or unique genetic markers that this person has.
V/O:
The image and shape of the face is created and skin colour added. In constructing a face they ask a simple question.
Ellen:
What is different, what is unique about this person’s face and these rainbow faces shows those differences
V/O:
Blue shows where a feature is less expressed than in the standard face and red where a feature is more prominent.
Ellen:
You see that the nose and brow is higher set on the face so we know it is a narrower longer face and then we have a slightly more protruding mouth as well.
V/O:
All of this helps to create a face based on the DNA alone. The powerful software makes it possible to manipulate the various feature in line with the DNA. Here the artist is manipulating a nose. He can also add skin colour, hair colour and eye colour to the basic face shape. And this is the result.
Ellen
We emphasize that this is really intended to be a description of this person and the vast majority of people in the world are not going to match this prediction. But some people will and if those people on your suspects list have a reason, you know, means motive and opportunity, then maybe then this is your person.
V/O:
The technology has been welcomed by law enforcement all over the world, and in addition to finding suspects, it is also used to identify and give a face to skeletal remains.

An analysis takes about a month, and it is time for our results to arrive.
Devi:
Well the results are in. I have just received this rather lengthy report. They are able to predict my eye colour, hair colour, skin colour and facial features just by using the 4 swabs we sent them. Let’s look at skin colour.
V/O:
The report is very precise and with 95,7% confidence they predict that my skin colour will be brown or light brown.
Devi:
Let’s see what they say about the colour of my eyes.
V/O:
With a confidence factor of 95,2% the report predicts that my eyes will be very dark brown.
Devi:
And now for my hair colour.
V/O:
The team predicts that I have very dark hair.
Devi:
They say that with a 99,9% confidence that my hair colour is black. They are absolutely right my original hair colour is black.

They are also able to say if you have freckles or not.
V/O:
In my case they are certain I have no freckles – and again they are correct.
Devi:
The report also includes information on my ethnic origins and ancestry and according to them I come from Central Asia. But what is even more interesting is that they are able to narrow it down to the Southern part of India, the part where Tamil people come from. And that is the story I have been told my entire life.
Devi:
And now for the highlight– what do I look like according to them.
V/O:
The face morphology analysis describes my features, and this leads to the creation of a likeness based on what the DNA has predicted.
Devi:
And this is the predicted picture, aged at about 25, and I must say, I am quite astounded, I did look like that.
V/O:
However, the image is not a photograph of the person. It is rather to be treated as an advanced identikit but in colour.
Lobo:
It is an absolute game changer………..whom you are not looking for.

Whereas traditional DNA forensics matches STRs from a sample to a known suspect or a database, DNA phenotyping can generate new leads about an individual, even if they have not previously been identified in a database.
metadata.Further information: DNA Phenotyping is the prediction of physical appearance from DNA. It can be used to generate leads in cases where there are no suspects or database hits, to narrow suspect lists, and to help solve human remains cases. Whereas traditional DNA forensics matches STRs from a sample to a known suspect or a database, DNA phenotyping can generate new leads about an individual, even if they have not previously been identified in a database. DNA phenotyping takes advantage of modern SNP technology to read the parts of the genome that actually code for the differences between people. The Snapshot DNA Phenotyping System translates SNP information from an unknown individual's DNA sample into predictions of ancestry and physical appearance traits, such as skin color, hair color, eye color, freckling, and even face morphology. Each phenotype prediction is made with a measure of confidence, including those that can be excluded with high confidence. SNP Technology. Recent advances in genomic technology have made it practical and affordable to read the sequence of millions of pieces of DNA from a small quantity of sample. This data captures a large proportion of the genomic variation between people and thus contains much of the genetic blueprint that differentiates people's appearance. These SNP genotypes can then be paired with phenotypes from thousands of subjects to create a genotype-and-phenotype (GaP) dataset for analysis. DNA Matching is a powerful feature that uses your DNA to help you find relatives. The technology compares your DNA data with the DNA data of others, and identifies shared genetic sequences that indicate a possible family relationship. The higher the percentage of DNA that you have in common with another person, the closer your likely relationship. All of this is now being used in the fight against crime and has been solving decades old cold cases over the last few months. Parabon NanoLabs, Inc. is a vertically integrated DNA technology company that develops next-generation therapeutic and forensic products, which leverage the enormous power of DNA. Staffed by a uniquely qualified team of scientists and technologists, with expertise ranging from bioinformatics and oncology to chemistry and computer science, the Company is bringing to market revolutionary new products and services made possible by recent advances in DNA sequencing, processing and manufacturing technologies. The are also the leaders in DNA sequencing and forensics and have developed the snapshot technology. Snapshot is a cutting-edge forensic DNA analysis service that provides a variety of tools for solving hard cases quickly: * Genetic Genealogy: Identify a subject by matching their DNA to one or more family members. * DNA Phenotyping: Predict physical appearance and ancestry of an unknown person from their DNA. * Kinship Inference: Determine kinship between DNA samples out to six degrees of relatedness. Snapshot is ideal for generating investigative leads, narrowing suspect lists, and solving human remains cases, without wasting time and money chasing false leads. We will also test the Snapshot technology by supplying them with DNA form Devi and see how they reconstruct the face. To make it local, we will also have Lobo das Neves to comment on the technology.
